title: Artificial Intelligence in Today’s Education Landscape: Understanding and Managing Ethical Issues for Educational Assessment
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the ethical issues that arise when artificial intelligence is used in educational assessment. The authors argue that although AI can support assessment practices, there is a need to understand the boundary between ethically permissible and impermissible uses, especially given concerns such as fairness, privacy, cheating, bias, and inclusivity.

To investigate this, the paper uses a systematic literature mapping approach over 33 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018 onward. The review searches Scopus, applies PRISMA-based screening, and uses topic modelling and network analysis to identify major application areas and ethical issue clusters. The study is not an intervention study in a single classroom or school; rather, it synthesizes the broader literature on AI-enabled assessment systems, including assessment construction, personalized feedback, automated grading, proctoring, predictive analytics, and learning intervention.

The paper finds fourteen recurring AI use-case themes and ten ethical issue themes. It concludes that AI-based assessment research is highly interdisciplinary and still early in development, with computer science and education both prominent. The authors emphasize that effective and appropriate AI use in assessments requires explicit ethics governance, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and practical mitigation measures tailored to specific assessment contexts.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Computer-aided instruction or assessment systems that use AI techniques to support instruction, assessment, feedback, grading, or related educational tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a systematic literature mapping of AI applications in educational assessment, including automated grading, personalized feedback, intelligent tutoring, proctoring, and related assessment functions across K-12 and other educational contexts.

findings.finding_summary: Across the 33 included studies, the review identified 14 AI application sub-themes in assessment, with the most cited uses being AI-generated personalized feedback (55%), AI-derived learning intervention/assistance (52%), AI-based assessment construction/curation/delivery (45%), and AI-facilitated response and grading (30%). The paper synthesizes these as common mechanisms through which AI is integrated into assessment workflows, rather than reporting a single experimental effect.
findings.measure: Frequency of AI assessment use cases across included studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic literature mapping/review rather than a primary intervention study. It synthesizes themes and frequencies across 33 papers, but does not report a controlled causal evaluation of one tool.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports descriptive prevalence of AI assessment uses, not effect sizes on learner outcomes. As a result, the practical impact of any single tool or intervention remains unclear from this review alone.
